methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $54M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
DeepDrive is a Series B transportation company that has raised $54.4M to date. The sector includes 8 private peers (Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Arc Boats, Parallel Systems, and others) and no public comparables. A narrow peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the transportation sector.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised ($54.4M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B progression yields an implied valuation of $103M. This reflects the expectation that Series B valuations advance materially from deployed capital, though the specific multiplier carries execution risk inherent to early-stage ventures.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $88M to $119M, with $103M as the central estimate. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression median. Key uncertainties include unit economics, capital efficiency relative to peer cohort, and the durability of the 1.9x multiplier in a frontier transportation market where comparables are sparse and heterogeneous. A multi-method triangulation would require either same-stage private peer financials or public market data—neither currently available—to reduce this range materially.
